tieu_de: Why does Spain own two cities in Africa?
chu_de: Why does Spain own two cities in Africa?

cau.chu: Spain still holds two African cities that Morocco claims.

su_that.trich: Ceuta (UK: , US: ; Spanish: [ˈθewta, ˈsewta] ; Moroccan Arabic: سَبْتَة, romanized: Sabtah) is an autonomous city of Spain on the North African coast.
Like the autonomous city of Ceuta and Spain's other territories along the northern African coast, Melilla is subject to an irredentist claim by Morocco.

cau.chu: Ceuta sits on the Strait of Gibraltar, bordered by Morocco.

su_that.trich: Bordered by Morocco, it lies between the Mediterranean Sea and the Atlantic Ocean.

cau.chu: In fourteen fifteen, Portugal seized Ceuta with forty five thousand men on two hundred ships.

su_that.trich: On the morning of 21 August 1415, King John I of Portugal led his sons and their assembled forces in a surprise assault that would come to be known as the Conquest of Ceuta. The 45,000 Portuguese who traveled on 200 ships caught the defenders of Ceuta off guard and suffered only eight casualties.

cau.chu: In sixteen forty, Ceuta chose to stay with Spain while Portugal broke away.

su_that.trich: In 1580, it was annexed by the Hispanic Monarchy, and the city chose to remain under Spanish authority after 1640.

cau.chu: On January first, sixteen sixty eight, Portugal formally ceded Ceuta to Spain.

su_that.trich: On 1 January 1668, King Afonso VI of Portugal recognised the formal allegiance of Ceuta to Spain and ceded Ceuta to King Carlos II of Spain by the Treaty of Lisbon.

cau.chu: Then Morocco laid siege to Ceuta for thirty three years, the longest siege in history.

su_that.trich: The city was attacked by Moroccan forces under Moulay Ismail during the Siege of Ceuta (1694–1727), the longest siege in history.

cau.chu: In fourteen ninety seven, Castile seized Melilla almost without a fight.

su_that.trich: Melilla was occupied on 17 September 1497, virtually without violence as it was on the border between the Kingdom of Tlemcen and the Kingdom of Fez, and as a result had been fought over many times and left abandoned.

cau.chu: In eighteen sixty, the Treaty of Wad Ras expanded both borders.

su_that.trich: The subsequent 1860 Treaty of Wad Ras expanded the borders of the Spanish plazas de soberanía.

cau.chu: In nineteen fifty six, Spain gave up Spanish Morocco but kept these two cities.

su_that.trich: When Spain recognized the independence of Spanish Morocco in 1956, Ceuta and the other plazas de soberanía remained under Spanish rule.
Melilla (, Spanish: [meˈliʝa] ; Tarifit: Mřič) is an autonomous city of Spain on the North African coast.

cau.chu: Morocco still disputes the Spanish claim, so why has Spain held on for centuries?

su_that.trich: Spain considered them integral parts of the Spanish state, but the Moroccan state has disputed this claim.
Ceuta belonged to the Spanish province of Cádiz as a regular municipality until the passage of its Statute of Autonomy in March 1995, when it became an autonomous city.
